findings.title: Styler reads parent record state stored in a widget property
findings.message: The split-button owner property is set on every Row widget. In the divider styling, `owner.node` is read from a record that can be replaced or stale, and `r.node.ID` comparisons run on every Button/MenuButton styler pass. In styleSplitButtonLayout, a Row child of a SplitButtonLayout row that is itself a Row also gets its Margin zeroed via the first branch only if SplitButtonLayout is set, but the parent check relies on a Property stored by pointer to a record whose `node` field is mutated during sync. This is racy if styling runs off the sync path.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the owner through a stable lookup, or store the SplitButtonLayout flag on the child records during sync so styling does not read the parent record's mutable node.

findings.title: Split-button validation order produces misleading errors
findings.message: The borderless/transparent check runs before the structural check and for any node with SplitButtonLayout set. A user who sets Style.Border on a segment gets a misleading error, and a malformed node (wrong kind) can hit the wrong message first. Ordering the checks incorrectly gives confusing errors, and the first check also runs when Kind isn't Row.
findings.suggestion: Perform the structural validation first, then the segment style validation.
